title: Repeating parts of text instead of transcribing - more than an hour long files
body:
It sometimes happpens that output looks like below. For some reason it stops transcribing and just repeats last part for 14 minutes, in this case. Any idea what can cause this? There is nothing special in the file that i could hear what could cause this.
It is pretty weird because otherwise it is amazingly good, sometimes even detecting songs being played. Are there any settings to adjust to prevent this?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I also noticed these repetitions.

I did some tests (using the ggml-medium.bin model) on some audio from an episode of an Italian TV series (about 32 minutes). There are ambient noises and music, sometimes even in the background during speeches. Maybe the problem could be traced back to this.
It seems that the phrase **following** the noises (or the music, if it is not recognised as such) is repeated for all the duration of these noises (I can provide an audio sample for this).
Maybe the repeating part starts in a similar situation and, for some reason, it continues for all the duration of the audio.

P.S.
Another thing I noticed that I did not expect (but which may be normal, I don't know) is that the windows executable downloaded from this page and the one for AARM64 compiled for macOS by my colleague, do not produce exactly the same transcription when I use the same audio on the same model.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: BTW I've seen this issue using upstream/pytorch Whisper on long video files.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Has anybody tried replicating the repeated lines problem with any up-to-date version of Whisper since OpenAI added this commit?

https://github.com/openai/whisper/commit/919a713499d4c4f76ecf448617ada8e9ac008fbb

This fix has been included since Whisper `20230307`.

The repeating/dupe line problems makes this very hard to use for anything non-English, and even then it can still break down and start looping very easily, so I would love to see if this fixes it.

comments.author: participant12
comments.body:
Same issue, repeated or looping text on translating to English. Workaround for me was splitting the wav file into segments of a couple minutes then writing a bash script to run whisper.cpp for all of them.

Not a real solution however.

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
I had some success with using

`-mc 100`

Which changes the maximum context. `-mc 10` made some sentences not look great, while `-mc 1000` showed the same problem again.

OK, sometimes `-mc 50` works better, sometimes it's `-mc 200`... But probably your only option for long files (more than  10-20 minutes) is to split them up :(

What worked on all my files so far is

`-mc 50 -bs 6 -bo 6 -tp 0.2`

But the quality is definitely lower than with `-mc 0`. Except that it doesn't have repetitions...

comments.author: participant14
comments.body:
I still have this problem with the latest git using CUDA, although I'm trying to use the CPU only to see if it changes anything.

I thought it was because I was using large-v3-turbo, but the problem is also there with large-v3.

Haven't tried any of the parameters @participant13 did, but it shouldn't happen with default options anyway right?

It seems the problem is more pronounced with big files

comments.author: participant14
comments.body: Interestingly, the CPU-only run is even worse! It starts repeating from 1 h 13 min up until the end, while the CUDA run is on the same input and with the same model, it starts repeating at 1h 48 min.

comments.author: participant14
comments.body:
The problem is definitely worse with large-v3 compared to large-v3-turbo. Had to revert after I saw many videos transcribed with repeating subtitles up until the end.

It might also be related to auto language detection. It might detect the wrong language and then get stuck somewhere.
But when language is set, it seems it happens more with Portuguese compared to English.
